# Simulation results (auto-generated)

**ASSUMPTION-DRIVEN comparison of rebalancing policies on a replica of the real network. Not an estimate of real savings.** Generated by `src/simulate/run_empirical.py`. Interpretation: `docs/simulation_findings.md`.

## E1. What was estimated from the data

Counted pickups and returns are lower bounds on true trips. Jumps of 8 bikes or more in one step are treated as truck moves and left out of the rates; their daily count is shown for context on the size of real rebalancing.

## E2. Forecast noise matched to the measured forecast accuracy

In the simulator the forecast predicts net bike outflow over the next H hours with added noise (sd in bikes). The noise is chosen so that 'projected level' ranks stations by risk of hitting zero within H hours with the same AUC the real gradient-boosted model achieved in the backtest (docs/forecast_results*.md). Matching is by ranking skill only; the real forecast and the simulated one predict different quantities, so treat this as a rough translation.

| horizon_h | measured_auc | noise_sd_bikes | auc_with_no_noise | auc_reactive_current_count_only | stockout_event_rate | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.9294 | 0 | 0.9112 | 0.9 | 0.0735 | target AUC is not reachable even with no forecast noise; using noise 0 |
| 3 | 0.8076 | 1.963 | 0.8331 | 0.8298 | 0.1518 |  |
| 6 | 0.7076 | 6.575 | 0.8027 | 0.7729 | 0.2375 |  |

## E2b. Does the simulated network resemble the real one? (validation)

Real = the frozen dataset's headline shares (which include whatever rebalancing the operator really does). Simulated = no rebalancing at all, end-of-hour states averaged over simulated days. **The simulation understates how often stations are empty**, so absolute lost-pickup numbers below should not be read as real; only relative comparisons between policies are meaningful, and even those are assumption-bound.

| measure | real | simulated_no_rebalancing |
|---|---|---|
| share of station-time empty | 0.1284 | 0.0774 |
| share of station-time full | 0.0632 | 0.0599 |
| mean bikes per station | 6.993 | 7.37 |

### Do simulated stations rank like real ones?

| measure | spearman_across_stations | stations |
|---|---|---|
| empty | 0.839 | 272 |
| full | 0.864 | 272 |
| mean_bikes | 0.904 | 272 |

## E3. Baseline scenario (demand scale 1.0, 6 transfers per round, 100 replications, 5 simulated days each)

Lost pickups = riders who wanted a bike at an empty station. 'avoided' = reduction versus no rebalancing, paired by replication; the interval is a 95% confidence interval for the AVERAGE over replications; sd_across_replications shows how much a single 5-day run varies.

| policy | service_level | lost_pickups_per_day | stockout_station_hours_per_day | transfers_per_day | avoided_vs_none | avoided_ci_lo | avoided_ci_hi | sd_across_replications |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 0.7982 | 2605 | 528.9 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| static | 0.8 | 2582 | 520.1 | 18.24 | 22.62 | 18.64 | 26.6 | 20.3 |
| reactive | 0.8056 | 2512 | 503.9 | 24 | 92.85 | 85.55 | 100.1 | 37.24 |
| forecast_1h | 0.8069 | 2495 | 500.4 | 24 | 109.8 | 103.2 | 116.3 | 33.51 |
| forecast_3h | 0.8081 | 2479 | 499.7 | 23.58 | 125.6 | 118.8 | 132.5 | 34.83 |
| forecast_6h | 0.8012 | 2568 | 511.4 | 19.87 | 37.08 | 30.42 | 43.74 | 33.99 |
| oracle_3h | 0.8091 | 2467 | 498 | 23.66 | 138 | 131.2 | 144.7 | 34.54 |

### E3b. Does forecasting add anything beyond reacting to current counts?

Positive = fewer lost pickups per day than the reactive policy. Interval = 95% confidence interval for the average.

| static | -70.23 | -77.89 | -62.58 |
| forecast_1h | 16.92 | 12.34 | 21.49 |
| forecast_3h | 32.78 | 26.25 | 39.31 |
| forecast_6h | -55.77 | -63.06 | -48.49 |
| oracle_3h | 45.12 | 38.87 | 51.36 |
